cards.text: Saul set out for Damascus with letters to its synagogues, ready to take followers of Jesus to Jerusalem as prisoners, until Jesus Himself stopped him on the road (Acts 9:1-6). Now his sight is back, he's been baptized, and he's spending days with the very disciples he came to arrest (Acts 9:18-19). And he doesn't waste a minute: Saul promptly starts proclaiming Jesus.

cards.question: Where in Damascus does Saul start proclaiming Jesus?
In the synagogues of Damascus, Saul declares that Jesus is the Son of God.

cards.text: Now picture the people in those synagogues. They KNOW this man, and this man is up front preaching the very name he came to town to arrest people for.

cards.question: The people in Damascus who hear Saul preach Jesus are ___.

cards.text: They ask, "Isn’t this the man who wreaked havoc in Jerusalem on those who call on this name?" That's like the guy who spent years blasting a company in every group chat showing up in their uniform, handing out their flyers.

cards.question: Once the people in Damascus start asking questions, Saul gets quieter and keeps his head down.
Saul confounds the Jews living in Damascus. How does he do it?

answers.text: By proving that Jesus is the Christ
By showing the high priest's letters
By performing a sign in the street

cards.text: After many days, the Jews in Damascus conspire to kill Saul. He went from hunter to hunted, and friend, that is NOT a promotion anybody applies for.

cards.question: Saul finds out about the plot to kill him.

cards.text: Day and night, they watch the city gates, waiting for him. Strolling out the front door of Damascus is off the table.

cards.question: The gates of Damascus are watched day and night. How do Saul's disciples get him out of the city one night?

answers.text: In a basket through a window

cards.text: Saul makes it to Jerusalem and tries to join the disciples there. Now, how's THAT gonna go?

cards.question: Saul tries to join the disciples in Jerusalem. How do they respond?

answers.text: They are all afraid of him

cards.question: The disciples in Jerusalem believe Saul is truly a disciple now.

cards.text: Then Barnabas steps in, a Levite from Cyprus whose name means Son of Encouragement (Acts 4:36). Friend, that man is about to EARN that name.

cards.question: Barnabas brings Saul to the ___ in Jerusalem.
Barnabas tells the apostles how Saul saw the Lord, who spoke to him on the road to Damascus. What else does Barnabas tell them about Saul?

answers.text: How he spoke boldly in Damascus
How he healed a blind man
How he fasted for forty days

cards.text: So Saul stays with them, moving about freely in Jerusalem and speaking boldly in the name of the Lord. One good word from the right person, and the guy everybody was dodging is now on the guest list.
Saul talks and debates with the Grecian Jews, Jews who speak Greek. Back and forth, back and forth.

cards.question: The Grecian Jews Saul debates with in Jerusalem try to kill him.

cards.text: When the brothers learn of this, they get Saul out of there, down to Caesarea.

cards.question: From Caesarea, the brothers send Saul off. Which city is he headed to?

cards.text: Then the church throughout Judea, Galilee and Samaria grows in strength and numbers, living in the fear of the Lord and the encouragement of the Holy Spirit. From a man in a basket to a whole church on the MOVE, friend.

cards.question: The church throughout Judea, Galilee and Samaria grows and is encouraged by the Holy Spirit. What kind of time does it experience?
